summary: This note covers the 2008 NBA draft, which broke with draft history by having the first three picks all be freshmen. Chicago took Derrick Rose first overall, Miami took Michael Beasley second, and Minnesota took O. J. Mayo third. The draft also set records for the most freshmen drafted and tied a record for players selected in the first two rounds from a single school.
one_line: The 2008 NBA draft, in which the first three picks were all freshmen, led by Derrick Rose going first overall to Chicago.
key_facts: For the first time in draft history, the first three draft picks were all freshmen.
The Chicago Bulls used the first overall pick in the 2008 NBA draft to select Derrick Rose from the University of Memphis.
Derrick Rose was a Chicago native.
Derrick Rose later won the NBA Rookie of the Year Award.
Derrick Rose was the first player since LeBron James in 2003 to be drafted first overall and win Rookie of the Year.
The Miami Heat used the second pick in the 2008 NBA draft to select Michael Beasley from Kansas State University.
The Minnesota Timberwolves used the third pick in the 2008 NBA draft to select O. J. Mayo from University of Southern California.
Five players from the University of Kansas were taken in the 2008 draft.
The University of Kansas tied University of Connecticut (2006) and University of Florida (2007) for the record most players selected in the first two rounds of an NBA draft.
Twelve freshmen were drafted in 2008, a record at the time.
Ten of the twelve freshmen drafted in 2008 were selected in the first round.
Of the players drafted in 2008, 29 are forwards.
Of the players drafted in 2008, 19 are guards.
Of the players drafted in 2008, 12 are centers.
